translations.title: How can sparse-reward sports training avoid a policy that falls before it ever reaches useful reward?
translations.answer: The OP3 soccer work first trains the minimum get-up and soccer skills, then uses state-routed teacher regularization to distill them into one policy and a historical snapshot pool to learn combination and competition. This addresses exploration and forgetting; it does not mean end-to-end self-play creates basic skills automatically, and small OP3 hardware limits do not transfer to full-size humanoids.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Get-up and ball-skill teachers are independently competent and frozen for distillation.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: A historical opponent evaluation pool is preserved separately from training.
translations.applicability.environments.0: 1v1 biped soccer with repeatable skill and set-piece tests
translations.applicability.robots.0: Robotis OP3 in the paper; full-size humanoids require different impact and safety evidence
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Paper training simulator with matched position-control and delay interface
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper's skill-prior/self-play ablations and fixed-count OP3 hardware tests support staged exploration and unified distillation. Confidence is capped because official code is unavailable, mocap supplies global state, and hardware evidence concerns a small protected platform.
translations.evidence.0.note: Shows separate soccer/get-up teachers, state-routed distillation, historical self-play, mechanism ablations, and quantified hardware skill/set-piece tests.
translations.evidence.0.title: Learning Agile Soccer Skills for a Bipedal Robot with Deep Reinforcement Learning
